description: Search the text inside digitised American newspaper pages held by the Library of Congress. This reads what optical recognition took off the scanned pages, so it finds a phrase that appears nowhere in a title or a catalogue record. Double quotes change how the Library matches the words, and it decides what they mean: a page can come back carrying the words apart or in another order rather than the phrase as written. What the quotes do to the number of matching pages varies from one query to the next, so run the search both ways rather than expecting either form to return more. 'total' counts the pages that match, and they page: ask for page 2, 3 and so on to see beyond the first answer. It is not a count of how many times the words occur. Each match names the newspaper, the date, the leaf of the issue and the state it was published in, and 'source_url' opens that leaf with the query applied. 'location' keeps to papers published in one state, 'publication' to a single paper, and 'year_from' with 'year_to' to a span of years. A filter matching nothing is dropped and the answer says so. Every match carries 'excerpt_kind', and the excerpts are labelled with it in the text. A 'passage' is the text around the words that matched. A 'page_opening' is the start of the page, sent because the text the Library returned with the row stops before those words appear, so it does not carry the match and quoting it quotes something else. Use search_items instead when looking for a work by its title, creator or subject.

location.description: The state a paper was published in, written as the Library writes it: 'new york', 'district of columbia'. It is the value 'state' carries on the matches this tool returns.

max_excerpt_chars.description: Budget for one passage. Read it together with 'max_excerpts_per_match': the size of the answer is the product of the two and the number of matches.

max_excerpts_per_match.description: Passages to keep per match. A page holding the words several times yields several, and the later ones rarely say anything the first did not.

publication.description: One newspaper, named with its town and the years it ran: 'new-york tribune (new york [n.y.]) 1866-1924'. Take the wording from 'publication' on a match here, or from a title in search_items with media_type 'newspapers'.

query.description: Words or a quoted phrase, such as '"cure for influenza"'. The index reads the text off the pages themselves and holds single characters, so a query of one character is a query it answers.

name: search_newspapers

creator.description: Whoever contributed the scan, which is a library.

excerpt_kind.description: 'passage' means the excerpts are the text around the words that matched, centred on them because they were found in the text returned with this row. 'page_opening' means they are the start of the page, sent because that text stops before the searched words appear, so a page_opening does not carry the match.

excerpts.description: Machine-read text off the page, all of the kind 'excerpt_kind' names.

identifier.description: Pass to get_item for the record of the issue this leaf belongs to.

publication.description: The newspaper, with the years it ran.

published_on.description: Date of the issue, as published.

source_url.description: Opens the leaf itself, with the query applied.

title.description: How the Library names the leaf, paper and date included.

total.description: Newspaper pages that match, not the number returned and not a count of occurrences. Raise 'page' to read further into it.

title: Search inside scanned newspaper pages
